correctness.rationale: All objects, m>=4, nonnegative independent floor parameters and boundaries are explicit. Convex automorphism averaging proves global reduction; Kronecker Laplacian diagonalization yields exactly three Fourier endpoint constraints. Each of five necessary inequalities is derived. The stated constructive weights satisfy all Fourier constraints and stochastic degree bound using a+b>=4, proving sufficiency without a numerical extrapolation. Strict facet examples prove four versus five essential pieces. Included standalone checker ran successfully: 1323 exact feasible floor pairs and 150 full-matrix Fourier-mode eigenvector checks on m=4,5,6. Computation supplements the all-m proof; no finite check asserted as infinite certification.

originality.rationale: Compared exact claimed two-floor value function, its pointwise constraints, attaining probabilities, and parity-dependent irredundancy against foundational FMMC SDPs, automorphism/product results, a same-graph prism spectrum paper, and a constrained FMMC paper on friendship graphs. value.rationale: Independent mandatory rim and rung transition rates naturally model obligatory local exploration and cross-layer connectivity on a canonical product network. The result gives the complete continuum of sharp SLEM bounds for every size and every feasible pair, explicit nonnegative attaining weights, and a nontrivial odd/even structural transition in the active holding-probability facet. This is a useful closed-form parametric graph optimization rather than an arbitrary finite slice or a generic SDP restatement.
